_what: Regression test for the U1 broker-health LED, both branches. Two faults are pinned here. (1) PRG_MQTT declared stMQTTInfo : MQTT.MQTT_INFO and read MQTT_CONNECTED off it, but nothing ever populated the struct, so the flag was FALSE for the whole history of the project and U1 never went green. (2) The falling-edge detector that was supposed to turn U1 red was called only from MQTT_INIT, which runs once, so its Q could never become TRUE. Both edge detectors are gone: U1 is written from a remembered state, bLedShowsHealthy, so there is one code path instead of two and no half of it can be left uncalled.
_why_two_flags: bBrokerHealthy is MQTT_CONNECTED AND GVL_MQTT.bBrokerReachable, and the second half is not redundant - it is the part a human found by pulling the cable. MQTT_CONNECTED does not notice a pulled network cable: TCP has nothing to report until a retransmit gives up, so the client holds a dead socket open for minutes and goes on claiming a session. Measured on this bench - LAN cable out, MQTT_CONNECTED still TRUE, U1 still green. PRG_PING_DMX now pings the broker every 10 s and writes bBrokerReachable.
_the_led_itself_is_not_readable: PFC.SetLed is a runtime call and no variable holds a colour, so bLedShowsHealthy is the closest thing to a read-back: it is what the code last wrote to U1. A person at the cabinet is still the only witness for the light. Verified by eye on the lab PFC200: cable out, U1 blinks red; cable back in, U1 returns to steady green.
_how_the_red_branch_is_driven: By pointing GVL_MQTT.broker at 192.0.2.1, which is RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 and guaranteed never to be a real host, so the ping genuinely fails. That exercises the whole shipping path - ICMP, the debounce, the flag, the health AND, the change detector and the real SetLed call - with nothing forced. It also reproduces the pulled-cable case faithfully, because the client ignores a URL change while its socket is up (tried and measured), so the MQTT session stays up and only reachability goes away.
_do_not_write_the_flag_instead: Writing GVL_MQTT.bBrokerReachable FALSE from the harness was the first attempt and it is racy: the Ping task rewrites the flag every 10 s, so the assertion is chasing a value another task owns. It failed exactly that way once. Drive the input, not the output.
_the_debounce_sets_the_waits: cuiBrokerPingFailsForRed is 2, so the red branch needs two failed 10 s cycles - hence 32 s in step 2, and 22 s in step 3 for the one success that clears it. uiBrokerPingFails is asserted at the threshold in step 2 to prove the counter saturates rather than running away.

steps.label: 1. THE GREEN BRANCH. Twelve seconds after a cold start the client has a session and the broker answers, so U1 is steady green. MQTT_CONNECTED reads FALSE here on the code before this fix - permanently, because nothing assigned stMQTTInfo. sBrokerHost also proves the port got stripped off GVL_MQTT.broker.

2. THE RED BRANCH. Point the ping at an address that cannot exist and U1 must go to blinking red - while the MQTT session is untouched and still reads connected, which is exactly what a pulled cable looks like and exactly what the old condition could not see.

3. and it heals on its own. One successful ping clears the counter, so the LED returns to steady green rather than latching red - and because nothing here writes the flag, a TRUE is the Ping task doing it, which makes this the test that the broker ping runs at all.
